title: Base change for an arbitrary morphism, against an open immersion
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ and the geometric data of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type carrying that ambient exceptional right adjoint datum, and let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to Y'$. On the ordinary derived categories of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the canonical exceptional base-change comparison
$$
\beta_f: Lg'^*Rf^\times\longrightarrow Rf'^\times Lg^*
$$
is an isomorphism. Here the adjoint for $f'$ is obtained using the base-changed compactification and the restricted FullCD bound. In particular this applies when $Y'$ is an affine open of $Y$.

Independently of the ambient datum, let $f:X\to Y$ be any separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion, and form the Cartesian square as above. For the finite coefficients of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], use the constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], interpreted by [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. For every coefficient sheaf $K$ of the etale-origin class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], regarded as a complex in degree zero, and also for every bounded constructible $K$ on $Y$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the canonical comparison
$$
Lg'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'^!Lg^*K
$$
is an isomorphism. This clause uses the relative adjunction on bounded-below complexes of etale origin; it does not assert the unrestricted ambient datum. It is this bounded-class comparison that affine-chart assembly consumes.

proof.text: For the conditional ambient assertion take the compactification $c=(j_0,p)$ and integer $c_{\mathrm{cd}}$ already included in [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. No Nagata theorem over the unrestricted base $S$ is required. The source $\overline X$ is finite type over $S$: $p$ is finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and finite type is preserved by composition. Concretely, over an affine base choose the finite affine covers in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; for each intermediate affine choose its finite affine preimage cover. If $B$ is generated by $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ over $R$ and $C$ by $c_1,\ldots,c_s$ over $B$, their images together generate $C$ over $R$. The resulting finite affine cover also gives quasi-compactness. This is the elementary affine-cover argument of Stacks Tag 01T3 (morphisms-lemma-composition-finite-type).

source.place: First sentence: use the compactification supplied by the hypothesis; finite-type prerequisites

proof.text: The identity-open compactification $(\mathrm{id}_{\overline X},p)$ has the same proper part and FullCD bound as $c$. Apply [lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint] over $S$ to it to obtain an ambient datum for $p$, including the proper adjunction $Rp_*\dashv Rp^\times$. Its geometric hypotheses hold by Step 1 and the given finite-type $Y\to S$; properness supplies separatedness. Keep the originally supplied datum for $f$.

source.place: Second sentence: supply the ambient-datum hypothesis for the proper part

proof.text: Base change $c$ along $g$, obtaining $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$, $j_0':X'\hookrightarrow\overline X'$, $p':\overline X'\to Y'$ and $\overline g:\overline X'\hookrightarrow\overline X$. The two open projections and $j_0'$ are open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and $p'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $p'j_0'=f'$ and $j_0g'=\overline g j_0'$. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $f'$ is separated finite type. Read the ambient geometric data for $f',p'$ over base $Y'$, so their sources and target are finite type over this base even when $g$ is not quasi-compact. The prime $\ell$ is invertible there because it is invertible on $S$.

source.place: First sentence: base-changed compactification and precise base scheme

proof.text: The original FullCD bound restricts to $p'$. For an arbitrary $A$-module sheaf $F'$ on $\overline X'$, put $F=\overline g_!F'$ as in [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Restricting its defining presheaf to objects over $\overline X'$ gives $F'$; sheafification commutes with slice restriction by [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification], so its sheafification also restricts to $F'$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $Y'\to Y$ is a site object and every site object $V\to Y'$ is a site object over $Y$. Apply clause 2 of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] to $F$, first at $Y'$ and then at each such $V$. The fibre products identify the resulting restrictions of $F$ with those of $F'$, so this proves both FullCD clauses for $p'$ with the same $c_{\mathrm{cd}}$. Apply [lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint] over $Y'$ to $(j_0',p')$ and $(\mathrm{id},p')$. This supplies the ambient datum for $f'$ and the proper adjunction for $p'$, with the refinement coherence that theorem states.

source.place: Second sentence: existence of the base-changed ambient adjunctions

proof.text: The conditional clause of [prop-exc-base-change-proper], applied to $p$ against $g$, gives the isomorphism $\beta_p:L\overline g^*Rp^\times\to Rp'^\times Lg^*$. Its ambient hypotheses were supplied in Steps 2 and 4. Apply [cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper] to $c$ and its pullback, the given ambient adjunction for $f$, the one just obtained for $f'$, and these proper adjunctions. Its specified mate-pasting implication gives invertibility of the canonical $\beta_f:Lg'^*Rf^\times\to Rf'^\times Lg^*$. This proves the first clause, including arbitrary open $g$.

source.place: Second and third sentences: proper comparison and reduction

proof.text: For the independent finite-field coefficient clause, $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y$ are Noetherian, and by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $Y$ is quasi-separated. Every open in a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. In particular the inverse image of each affine open under $g$ is quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes $g$ finite type. The finite-type composition argument of Step 1 makes $Y'$ finite type over $k$. Now [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to $f$ over the qcqs target $Y$, giving $c=(j_0,p)$. Its proper part has source finite type over $k$ by Step 1. Pull back $c$ as in Step 3; $\overline X'$ and $X'$ are open subschemes of Noetherian finite-type $k$-schemes, so the same quasi-compact-open and composition arguments make them finite type over $k$.

source.place: First sentence for the independent class clause: Nagata is used only over the Noetherian base

proof.text:
Choose nonnegative integral dimension bounds for $\overline X$ and $\overline X'$ using [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; the empty case permits bound $0$. Thus [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] applies to $f,f'$ and to the identity-open compactifications of $p,p'$. Use its bounded-below relative adjoints, denoted $R_f,R_{f'},R_p,R_{p'}$, with their stated formulas $R_h=
u^*h_{\mathrm{et}}^	imes R
u_*$. For a comparison-class input $L=
u_Y^*H$ with $H\in D^+$, [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies $R
u_*L$ with $H$. The etale output $h_{\mathrm{et}}^	imes H$ is bounded below by [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]: put $H$ at every level $m\geq n$ by restriction of scalars $A_m	o A_n$, with identity transitions and zero below $n$; the uniform lower bound for its system adjoint, evaluated at $n$, gives the bound for $h_n^	imes H$. Thus the formulas supply actual bounded-below etale-origin witnesses, not only boundedness of their pro-etale realizations. They are the finite exceptional inverse images of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. As [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge] expressly states, this supplies the relative adjunction; it supplies no unrestricted ambient datum. No use of the conditional clause of Step 5 is made in this independent argument.

source.place: Independent class sentence, interpreted with the actual statement of the discharge corollary

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C_T=\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(T,A)$ be the induced full category with witnesses of [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. All open functors in the diagram restrict to these categories. For restriction along an open $u:U\hookrightarrow T$, apply [lem-sf-fullcd-class-restriction] with $\overline X=Y=T$, $f=\mathrm{id}_T$, $V=U$, and $v=u$. Its natural sheaf isomorphism gives $u^*\nu_T^*H\cong\nu_U^*u_{\mathrm{et}}^*H$ termwise. Exactness of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] makes this an isomorphism on bounded-below complexes; [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] supplies the exactness of etale module restriction and hence its preservation of the lower bound. For extension by zero use the natural comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] termwise; [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] supply the respective exactness statements and preservation of the lower bound. These constructions transport the witnesses, and their maps are the underlying ambient functor maps because $\mathcal C_T$ is induced. Finally [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] puts $Rp_*j_{0!}$ and its primed version in the target comparison class; with identity open it does the same for $Rp_*,Rp'_*$.

source.place: Independent class sentence: check the domains of every adjunction before pasting

proof.text:
On these full comparison categories [prop-exc-open-adjoint] restricts to $j_{0!}\dashv j_0^*$ and $j'_{0!}\dashv j_0'^*$. The relative Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] restrict to genuine adjunctions $Rp_*\dashv R_p$, $Rp'_*\dashv R_{p'}$, $Rp_*j_{0!}\dashv R_f$ and $Rp'_*j'_{0!}\dashv R_{f'}$, since Step 8 verifies that all these functors land in the indicated full categories. Apply [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] to obtain unit/counit-compatible isomorphisms
$$\rho:R_f\xrightarrow{\sim}j_0^*R_p,\qquad \rho':R_{f'}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_0'^*R_{p'}.$$
Thus the proper-to-general reduction can be performed within these categories; no extension of a relative adjunction to all pro-etale objects is involved.

source.place: Third sentence on the comparison class: compose the proper and open adjunctions

proof.text:
Apply the independent relative clause of [prop-exc-base-change-proper] to the proper part $p$ and $g$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\beta_p:\overline g^*R_p\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{p'}g^*$ on bounded-below etale-origin inputs. The coefficient, finite-type and bounded-below hypotheses are exactly Steps 6-8. The canonical composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $(g',j_0)$ and $(j_0',\overline g)$ give
$$\alpha:g'^*j_0^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_0'^*\overline g^*.$$
The structure maps of the constant coefficient sheaves send $a\in A$ to the same constant $a$, so the two coefficient identifications agree. Pullbacks here equal their derived pullbacks by the exactness in Step 8. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], let $\delta_p:Rp'_*\overline g^*\to g^*Rp_*$ be the inverse mate of this specified $\beta_p$, and $\gamma:j'_{0!}g'^*\to\overline g^*j_{0!}$ the inverse mate of $\alpha$.

source.place: Second sentence for the relative class: proper comparison and upper open square

proof.text:
Define the pasted support square by
$$\delta_f=(\delta_pj_{0!})\circ(Rp'_*\gamma):Rp'_*j'_{0!}g'^*\to g^*Rp_*j_{0!}.$$
Its mate is the canonical relative exceptional comparison, with the proper square normalized by Step 10 and the open square by pullback composition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) with $(L_1,L_2,L_3,L_4)=(j_{0!},j'_{0!},Rp_*,Rp'_*)$ and horizontal functors $(g'^*,\overline g^*,g^*)$. Clauses (2) and (3), together with the unit/counit-compatible $\rho,\rho'$ of Step 9, give componentwise
$$\rho'_{g^*L}\,\beta_{f,L}=j_0'^*(\beta_{p,L})\,\alpha_{R_pL}\,g'^*(\rho_L).$$
This is an equality for the specified mates, not just an isomorphism of their endpoints. It is exactly the proper-then-open pasting in the blueprint proof, now using only genuine adjunctions on the comparison categories.

source.place: Third sentence for the relative class: explicit mate pasting and normalization

proof.text: Solve the equation of Step 11 for $\beta_{f,L}$ by multiplying on the left by $(\rho'_{g^*L})^{-1}$. All four resulting factors are invertible: $\rho,\rho',\alpha$ are isomorphisms, $\beta_p$ is an isomorphism by Step 10, and a functor preserves inverse pairs because it preserves composition and identities. Reversing the factors and replacing each by its inverse gives an inverse to $\beta_{f,L}$. Therefore the comparison is an isomorphism on the whole bounded-below etale-origin class. A sheaf in [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], placed in degree zero, has the required witness. Bounded constructible complexes have such witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Substituting $R_f=Rf^!$ from Step 7 proves exactly the two classes of inputs in the independent clause. Finally an affine-open inclusion is an open immersion, so the same comparison gives the asserted affine-chart specialization.

source.place: Conclusion: invert the comparison, verify the two input classes, and specialize to affine opens

The STATEMENT-DISPUTED is correct: the blueprint says the ambient datum is cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge, but that corollary explicitly does not assert it, and the blueprint's own warnings give the elliptic-curve counterexample (A=F_r). The two-clause statement is kept, so nothing is weakened. Clause 1: the datum's own compactification is used (Nagata over an arbitrary S would need qcqs). For FullCD(p'), extension by zero, lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification and the weakly-etale localization lemma correctly turn FullCD(p) clause 2 at V=Y' and at V->Y' into both clauses for p'. prop-exc-base-change-proper and cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper then apply; that the datum over S is also one over Y is implicit but elementary. Clause 2: Noetherianity makes g finite type, so Nagata applies over a qcqs Y. The C_T=D^+_et categories are closed under open restriction, extension by zero and compact support. Step 7's lower-bound argument gives real etale witnesses. I checked the mate orientations of delta_p, gamma and alpha against def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, and lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting(2),(3) with (j0!,j0'!,Rp_*,Rp'_*), (g'^*,gbar^*,g^*), sigma=tau=id gives exactly the displayed formula for beta_f. blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type carrying the ambient exceptional
right adjoint datum of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], and let
$g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an *open immersion*. Then the
base-change comparison $Lg'^*Rf^{\times}\to Rf'^{\times}Lg^*$ is an
isomorphism. In particular the base-change comparison holds for the
passage from an affine open of the base to the base, which is what an
assembly on affine charts requires. On the blueprint's coefficient class
[def-sf-fullcd-used-class] the ambient datum displayed as the hypothesis
is the theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge], so the comparison is
an isomorphism on that class without hypothesis.

proof.text:
Choose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$
of [thm-nagata-compactification], with $p$ proper. By
[prop-exc-base-change-proper] the comparison holds for $p$ against
the open immersion $g$, and by
[cor-exc-base-change-reduces-to-proper] the comparison for $f$
follows from that for $p$.
